SplitCompare.use: 16:9 two-sided contrast of one memory or bandwidth figure against another. pipes: two panels side by side, each with a memory block (orange) and a compute block (blue) joined by a data pipe; the left pipe is a narrow 2-lane pipe where packets queue, the right pipe is much wider (ratio times the lanes) and flows freely. panels: two big value cards side by side (title, big value, sub). Use pipes to show that one side is bandwidth-starved and the other is wide; use panels to compare two headline numbers.

props.mode: pipes (left narrow vs right wide data pipe) | panels (two value panels)
props.left: {title, value, sub, color} for the left panel; color is blue | orange | green | red | gray
props.right: {title, value, sub, color} for the right panel; color is blue | orange | green | red | gray
props.ratio: right pipe width / left, pipes only (default 8, right gets round(2*ratio) lanes, max 24)

SplitCompare.beats: reveal: right side highlighted (yellow border; in panels mode the right card also scales up 4 %)

HBars.use: 16:9 horizontal bar chart of up to 6 labelled values, bars grow one after another from the left. Use to compare sizes, capacities or speeds across a few options (for example model size per quantisation level, or memory per precision). One row can be highlighted as the answer.

props.items: list of up to 6 {label (str), value (number), text (str shown at bar end, default value plus unit), color (blue | orange | green | red | gray, default green)}
props.unit: str appended to the default bar-end text, for example GB
props.highlight: row index to highlight (default -1 for given items; with no items prop the default is 2)
props.note: short caption at the top right, 30 px

HBars.beats: reveal: highlighted bar gets a yellow outline and the others dim to 45 %; impact: highlighted bar pulses once

ChipTags.use: 16:9 chip die diagram with labels attached to places on the chip: an NPU block, Cache and MC blocks inside the die, and an orange LPDDR block outside its right edge. Tags pop in one at a time, each linked by a leader line to its own point on the die, so they read as annotations of the chip, not as a list. Use to name the parts or features of an accelerator or SoC (KV cache, runtime, kernel, power, thermal) and to show which parts are involved.

props.tags: list of up to 8 short labels, default [KV Cache, Cache 命中率, Runtime, Kernel, 功耗, 散热]
props.emphasis: index of the tag to highlight with a yellow border on impact (default -1 = none)

ChipTags.beats: reveal: the first tag appears (later tags 0.45 s apart); impact: the emphasis tag border turns yellow
